t: You're in the old City and Liberty of Westminster, a former unit of local government in Middlesex, just west of the City of London. It began under the control of Westminster Abbey, and from 1585 to 1900 it was run by the Westminster Court of Burgesses. Today it forms the southern part of the City of Westminster. Several notable people are linked to the area. The poet and essayist Bonnell Thornton was born here, and went on to Westminster School and Oxford. Sir William Dawes, Archbishop of York, died here, as did the Loyalist judge William Browne, later governor of Bermuda.
